answer: Quill-based identity verification requires an operator to physically possess a single quill to sign each new identity, so one person cannot create multiple accounts without owning many quills. The enforcement rule requires per-identity hardware purchase, costing an attacker a real quill for every new account. This system functions as a stark oasis where only those with genuine resources can proceed. Each identity is stored in a secure vault, ensuring the per-identity cost remains unchanged.
